definitions.explanation: A refined, old-fashioned greeting used both when meeting and when parting, wishing the other person well. Associated with upper-class speech and girls' schools; rare in everyday conversation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{皆様|みなさま}→皆様：15860_minasama⟧、ご{機嫌|きげん}よう。

⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{生徒|せいと}→生徒：01051_seito⟧⟦{同士|どうし}→同士：03474_doushi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧「ご{機嫌|きげん}よう」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{交|か}わす→交わす：19373_kawasu⟧。
examples.english: At that school, the students greet each other with "gokigenyō".

notes:
From ⟦ご{機嫌|きげん}→ご機嫌：25581_gokigen⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧ (in good spirits), as in ⟦ご{機嫌|きげん}→ご機嫌：25581_gokigen⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧お⟦{過|す}ごし→過ごす：02062_sugosu⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧ (stay well). Works for both hello and goodbye, like a refined "good day".

USAGE:
Heard at some private girls' schools, in period dramas, and in the speech of characters meant to sound elegant or aristocratic. In ordinary life it can sound affected or playful; people say ⟦こんにちは→こんにちは：02839_konnichiha⟧, ⟦さようなら→さようなら：10531_sayounara⟧ or {失礼|しつれい}します instead.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦さようなら→さようなら：10531_sayounara⟧: goodbye — the standard farewell
- お⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧で: take care — for a longer parting
